title: Multidimensional Emotional Assessment for Community Mental Health: Exploring Sample-Based Reference Values for the Core Seven-Emotions Inventory–Short Form (CSEI-s)
content:
Background/Objectives: Recognizing the types and intensity of everyday emotions helps people articulate distress and seek support. Community assessment therefore needs to describe coexisting emotions alongside specific symptoms. The Core Seven-Emotions Inventory–Short Form (CSEI-s), developed and initially validated in Korea, draws on traditional Korean medicine’s Seven Emotions framework. However, references for interpreting scores across adult age groups remain limited. This study explored sample-based references for multidimensional emotional profiles.
Methods: A cross-sectional online survey included 1,769 adults aged 20–65 years recruited through non-probability sampling across 17 Korean regions. Subscale percentile ranks, linear T scores, and measurement-error estimates were derived. Internal consistency, factor structure, and demographic differences were examined.
Results: Subscale Cronbach’s α ranged from 0.736 to 0.900. A score of 12 corresponded to percentile ranks of 48.8 for Rumination/Pensiveness and 82.5 for Anger. Older groups generally reported lower scores. Factor-model misfit and differential item functioning constrained interpretation.
Conclusions: These references enable subscale scores to be interpreted within a defined sample, providing a basis for describing everyday emotional profiles. They offer groundwork for developing and evaluating applications that support emotional self-understanding and communication in community mental-health education and primary care. The values are sample-based, non-diagnostic resources, rather than population norms or clinical thresholds.
